::: {.why}
This is the test that turns a claim about your engine into a fact about it, and it is the one an interviewer will ask you to describe.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement a test that corrupts all data after the decision timestamp and asserts every backtest output is bit-identical.
- Say what the test would fail to catch, and write a second test for that gap.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write tests/test_no_lookahead.py: run a strategy over a fixed window, then rerun it with every value after each decision timestamp replaced by noise, and assert the fills, positions and returns are identical. Run it against all your strategies. If any of them fails, the failure is the most valuable result of the week.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Find the gap: the poisoning test catches a strategy reading forward data, but it does not catch a parameter that was chosen by looking at the whole sample, because that choice happened outside the engine. Write the second test as an assertion that the configuration hash used in a run matches one recorded before the evaluation window began.
:::
:::

:::
